findings.location: “That was the straw that broke the camel’s back,” Becky said. “I became alarmed when I heard him yawning in the middle of the night and knew that he was not sleeping.”

findings.suggested_fix:
“I became alarmed” was translated as “התרעתי,” which means “I warned” or “I sounded an alarm” and changes the sense. Replace with wording that conveys Becky’s alarmed/distressed reaction. For example: “

“זה היה הקש ששבר את גב הגמל,” אמרה בקי. “נבהלתי כששמעתי אותו מפהק באמצע הלילה וידעתי שאינו ישן.”

findings.location:
Prolonged overload can be emotionally and mentally damaging

Intense, long-lasting pressures or troubles shouldered alone can cause severe stress. Minor stress is normal, but prolonged stress can cause depression, anxiety, heart disease, and high blood pressure. How you handle prolonged stress is important.
findings.source_quote: How you handle prolonged stress is important.
findings.suggested_fix: The Hebrew translation uses the masculine pronoun (“האופן שבו אתה מתמודד”), while the rest of the article addresses a female readership and several nearby imperatives are feminine. Use the feminine form to match register and audience. For example: replace “האופן שבו אתה מתמודד עם מתח ממושך הוא חשוב.” with “האופן שבו את מתמודדת עם מתח ממושך הוא חשוב.” Preserve tags and surrounding sentences.
